headline: Bangladesh, Kazakhstan agree to open embassies to boost ties
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Kazakh PM Oljas Bektenov discussed economic cooperation and diplomatic missions during the Summer Davos Forum in China.
details: Bangladesh and Kazakhstan have agreed to establish permanent diplomatic missions in their respective capitals to strengthen bilateral relations and economic cooperation.
The agreement was reached during a meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Kazakh Prime Minister Oljas Bektenov on Wednesday in Dalian, China.
The meeting took place on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting of the New Champions, also known as the Summer Davos Forum.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman advocated for stronger ties and regular interactions between government officials, business leaders, and citizens to enhance political and economic engagement.
PM Bektenov welcomed the prospect of greater commercial involvement and expressed optimism about expanding bilateral trade and investment.
The two leaders discussed potential partnerships in exporting skilled Bangladeshi workforce, renewable energy, digital infrastructure, technology, agribusiness, and food processing.
Kazakhstan proposed the creation of a specialized UN agency for water diplomacy, a move that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman confirmed Dhaka fully supports.
The meeting was attended by Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman, Foreign Affairs Advisor Humayun Kabir, and Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Ruman.
caption:
Bangladesh and Kazakhstan are set to open permanent embassies in their capitals to strengthen diplomatic and economic ties.

Bangladesh and Kazakhstan have agreed to establish permanent diplomatic missions in their respective capitals to strengthen bilateral relations and economic cooperation.

The agreement was reached during a meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Kazakh Prime Minister Oljas Bektenov on Wednesday in Dalian, China.

The meeting took place on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting of the New Champions, also known as the Summer Davos Forum.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman advocated for stronger ties and regular interactions between government officials, business leaders, and citizens to enhance political and economic engagement.

PM Bektenov welcomed the prospect of greater commercial involvement and expressed optimism about expanding bilateral trade and investment.

The two leaders discussed potential partnerships in exporting skilled Bangladeshi workforce, renewable energy, digital infrastructure, technology, agribusiness, and food processing.

Kazakhstan proposed the creation of a specialized UN agency for water diplomacy, a move that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman confirmed Dhaka fully supports.

The meeting was attended by Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman, Foreign Affairs Advisor Humayun Kabir, and Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Ruman.

headline: Youth beaten to death by mob in Tongi over mugging suspicion
summary: An unidentified man, estimated to be 22 years old, was killed by a crowd in Gazipur after being suspected of mugging.
details: An unidentified young man, believed to be around 22 years old, was beaten to death by a mob in Tongi, Gazipur, today.
The incident occurred around 7:00 am near the staircase leading to the Tongi–Abdullahpur Flyover from Station Road on the Dhaka–Mymensingh Highway.
According to Inspector (Investigation) Mohammad Zillur Rahman of Tongi East Police Station, local residents detained the youth on suspicion of mugging and assaulted him.
The victim died at the scene before police could intervene.
Police recovered the body and sent it to Shaheed Ahsan Ullah Master General Hospital in Tongi for further procedures.
Authorities are currently using fingerprints to identify the deceased.
Inspector Zillur stated that it is still under investigation whether the victim was actually involved in any mugging activity.
